name: Self-storage — drive-up
summary: Single-story pre-engineered metal buildings with exterior roll-up doors, separated by 25–30 ft paved drive aisles, fenced and gated. Building cost per SF is low, but paving, drainage and fencing are a large share because site coverage is only ~35–45%. Evidence: one vendor cost table and two announced Texas projects; default is a derived midpoint with low-medium confidence.

typicalSize.method: Announced Texas projects 91,200–128,900 SF (e2/e3); typical suburban drive-up facilities 40k–120k NRSF (judgment).

sfPerPrimaryUnit.method: Gross building SF per NRSF: exterior-access buildings have no corridors; only partitions, office and wall thickness are lost → ~89–96% efficiency (judgment).

primaryUnitsPerAcre.method: Building coverage ~30–45% of site (drive aisles 25–30 ft between rows, detention, setbacks) → 13,000–19,600 GSF/acre ÷ 1.08 ≈ 12,000–18,000 NRSF/acre; mid 16,000 (judgment).

parkingPerPrimaryUnit.method: Office parking only (≈ 4–8 spaces per facility); customers park at units in drive aisles.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Building: vendor single-story $55–$90/GSF construction only (e1; illustrative midpoint $72.50, e4); Austin expansion $60/SF (e2). Sitework added bottom-up: ~1.3–1.6 SF of paved aisle per GSF of building × ~$7–$12/SF for asphalt on base + drainage/fencing share (paving block asphalt $30–$70/SY ≈ $3.3–$7.8/SF plus base/drainage) ≈ $10–$18/GSF. Total ≈ $65–$108/GSF, consistent with Forney project $101/SF incl. canopies (e3). × 1.08 GSF/NRSF → ≈ $70–$117/NRSF; mid $80 (building $62 + site $12 = $74/GSF × 1.08), low $55 (Austin-type expansion, minimal sitework), high $115.

scope.notes: Contractor price incl. GC/OH&P; PEMB storage buildings with roll-up doors, small office/kiosk, drive-aisle paving, grading, detention, perimeter fence/gate, lighting and on-site utilities. Excludes land, soft costs, off-sites, fees and covered RV/boat canopies (see boat-rv-storage).

qualityTiers.method: economy ≈ low/mid (55/80 = 0.69); premium ≈ (mid+high)/2/mid = 1.22 rounded (concrete aisles, masonry façade); luxury ≈ high/mid (1.44).

systemSplit.method: No public elemental breakdown. Judgment: PEMB frame/girts 05 17%, metal roof/wall panels 07 8%, slab-on-grade 03 12%, roll-up doors 08 14%, partitions 10 3%, lighting/power 26 5%, gate/cameras 28 2%; sitework 31–33 28% (paving/aisles 17%, grading 7%, storm 4%) per the bottom-up site build-up in hardCost; GC 9%.

lineItems.name: Drive-aisle asphalt paving on aggregate base

cost.method: From _blocks/paving.json asphalt-paving ($30/$45/$70 per SY). Quantity ≈ 1.4 SF of paving per NRSF = 0.156 SY/NRSF (25–30 ft aisles between 30–40 ft deep building rows).

lineItems.notes: Carve-out; concrete aisles roughly double this.

lineItems.name: Perimeter security fence with keypad gate

cost.method: No public unit price fetched. 6–8 ft chain-link to ornamental steel fence $35–$110/LF incl. posts/footings, with automated gate allowance spread over the run (judgment). ~450 LF per acre for a 4–6 acre site (perimeter of a 5-acre square ≈ 1,870 LF; buildings often form part of the perimeter).

lineItems.name: Gate keypad, access control and CCTV

cost.method: Building-systems block access-control $1.5k–$4.5k per door (e7) and CCTV ~$1k–$3k per camera; drive-up sites need 1–2 gates + 20–35 cameras (judgment).

pctOfHard.method: Vendor guide uses 18% soft costs on a single-story example (e4) and 15–22% of total project cost generally (climate file e3); simpler single-story design → slightly below climate-controlled. Mid 17%.

softCosts.notes: Includes feasibility study and lease-up marketing; excludes financing.

perPrimaryUnit.method: min ≈ hard low $55 × 1.05; max ≈ hard high $115 × 1.3.

source.title: Self Storage Building Costs in 2026: A Comprehensive Guide

evidence.scopeNotes: Vendor blog citing Marcus & Millichap / C&W surveys without per-figure attribution; building only, no sitework.

evidence.quote: 9900 Darden Hill Road in Austin includes seven single-story buildings comprising a total of 91,200 square feet. The $5.5 million addition is expected to be complete in February.
evidence.scopeNotes: $5.5M / 91,200 SF = $60.31/SF for an expansion (Storelocal); likely building construction with limited new sitework.

evidence.quote: The $13 million project at 8078 FM 741 will contain five buildings comprising 128,900 square feet. It’ll also include two vehicle-storage canopy structures.
evidence.scopeNotes: $13M / 128,900 SF = $100.85/SF; "project" cost probably includes sitework, canopies and possibly soft costs/land; mix of building types not stated.
